name: Bugun
confidence_why: No source describes Bugun word stress: Lander-Portnoy 2013, the only phonological study, says stress is beyond its scope and that the role of tone and stress is still unknown, the second-hand tone claim it quotes from Dondrup 1990 fails Lander-Portnoy's own pitch measurements on two of three words, and Lieberherr and Bodt 2017 and Anderson and Harrison 2011 are silent on prosody.
catalog_citation: Dondrup, Rinchin. 1990. Bugun language guide. Itanagar: Directorate of Research, Government of Arunachal Pradesh. vi+101 pp. (OCLC 702433490).
catalog_locator: Part One: Phonology, heading 'TONE', pp. 2-3 (read). The contents page lists Part I Phonology as Consonants, Vowels, Dipthong, Nasalization and has no Stress or Accent heading; the phonology part (pp. 1-3, pp. 9-11) contains no statement on stress.
catalog_quote: TONE: Tone which has not been marked by any sign in this book has a distinctive feature of the language. The same word pronounced in different pitch differs in meaning. A list of such words is given below. Examples: kho (rising) —Omit / kho (falling) —Water / chau (rising) —Spit / chau (falling) —Cry / kua (rising) —Wear / kua (falling) —Five / chai (rising) —Dog / chai (falling) —Borrow

new_statements.rule_in_words: No source states where word stress falls. The only accessible phonological description (Lander-Portnoy 2013) explicitly leaves stress unstudied and says its role is unknown. The primary sketch (Dondrup 1990, quoted second-hand) claims Bugun has two contrastive tones, rising vs falling, with four minimal pairs; Lander-Portnoy's pitch measurements on three tokens contradict Dondrup in two of three and he calls the tone system erroneous or unproven. Barbora 2025 (paywalled) says its sketch covers 'tone'.
new_statements.exceptions: None; the tone claim itself is disputed (Lander-Portnoy 2013 pp. 28-29: 'Dondrup's system is erroneous either in its description of the tonal system in Bugun or fundamentally in its prediction of phonemic tones or pitches').
new_statements.domain_note: Monosyllabic citation forms (Dondrup's minimal pairs kho, chau, kua, chai); Lander-Portnoy's data are isolated words from the 2011 Enduring Voices recordings (Bugun Talking Dictionary). Nothing on phrase-level prosody.
new_statements.identity_note: Lander-Portnoy 2013 describes Bugun as recorded by the 2011 Enduring Voices expedition (village given as 'Rama Bao', possibly Ramu, Singchung circle); Lieberherr & Bodt 2017 distinguish Singchung and Bichom varieties; Barbora 2025 draws on three villages. All fall under bugu1246; no dialect-level glottocodes exist. Dondrup 1990 is the 'Handbook on Bugun Language Guide' named by the earlier scan.

tone_statements.citation: Blench, Roger. 2018. Introduction to Bugun. Preliminary draft (ms.), cited in Barbora 2025.
tone_statements.quote: The phonology of Bugun is quite similar to other languages in the area. Bugun has a large number of consonant clusters, as well as nasalised vowels, but a reduced tonal system, probably only contrasting Level and Rising. This paper presents a preliminary summary of the evidence to date.
tone_statements.summary: Author calls it a reduced tone system, 'probably' only Level vs Rising (hedged, preliminary draft); no further tone analysis; wordlist forms carry acute/grave marks (at least 40); nothing on stress.
